passage: With ten minutes left before the picnic bus left, Kashish grabbed Sachin's cap and tossed it between two friends, and everyone laughed. He liked that sound; it made him feel tall. Sachin stood by the bus door and said nothing, his eyes on his shoes, his lip pressed white. For a moment Kashish really saw that look, and remembered his elder brother doing the same to him at home while the family watched. His laugh dried up. The teacher was calling out names and time was short, but Kashish walked over, held out the cap and said, "Sorry. That wasn't funny." Sachin took it without a word. It was not enough, and Kashish knew it.

qa.q: What did Kashish do with Sachin's cap?
qa.a: He tossed it between two friends.

qa.q: Why did Kashish's laugh dry up after he looked at Sachin?
qa.a: He saw the hurt in Sachin's face and it reminded him of how his elder brother treated him at home, so the teasing no longer made him feel big.

qa.q: What made Kashish's apology a step in the right direction, and what more might he do?
qa.a: He stopped, returned the cap and said sorry plainly; he could also stay kinder from now on and ask himself why he wanted to feel big.

qa.q: How might Sachin see the apology?
qa.a: Sachin took the cap without a word, so he may still feel hurt or unsure it is real; an apology starts repair but does not fix things at once.

grounding: A child who teases a quieter boy for laughs notices his hurt, stops and apologises.

passage:
Rain had pushed PT indoors, and the hall was cramped and noisy. Raghav grabbed Mihir's water bottle and held it high. "Come on, shorty, jump!" The boys around him laughed, and Raghav felt ten feet tall. It was the same trick his older brother played on him at home every night.
Mihir jumped, missed, and stopped. His lips pressed tight and his eyes went shiny.
Raghav's arm stayed up, but something inside him dropped. He remembered that exact feeling from home.
Lalremsiami Ma'am was busy with the mats, too far to see. Raghav lowered the bottle himself. "Here. Sorry, Mihir. That wasn't funny." The laughter trailed off.

qa.q: What did Raghav grab from Mihir?
Why did something inside Raghav drop when he saw Mihir's eyes?
qa.a: He recognised the same hurt he feels when his brother teases him at home, and felt ashamed of doing it to someone else.

qa.q: What did Raghav do that showed real change?
qa.a: He noticed the hurt on Mihir's face, stopped on his own without a teacher seeing, and said sorry.

qa.q: How might Mihir have felt when Raghav held the bottle high?
qa.a: Mihir felt small and humiliated, pressing his lips tight while holding back tears.

grounding: A boy picks on a quieter boy to feel big and get laughs, copying how he is treated at home; seeing the hurt on the boy's face, he stops and apologises.

passage:
At the colony park in Pune, Suraj snatched Ansh's cricket cap and plonked it on his own head. "Look, it's the silent monk! Say something, monk!" Two boys laughed. Suraj felt big.
At home his cousin Seema called him "Chhotu" in front of guests, and everyone laughed. He hated it. Here, for once, he was the big one.
Then Ansh looked up. His chin trembled, the same way Suraj's did when the guests laughed.
Suraj stopped. His face grew hot. He took the cap off and handed it back. "Sorry, Ansh. I shouldn't have said that."
Ansh took the cap without a word. Suraj walked home slowly, thinking about Seema.

qa.q: What does Suraj's hot face suggest after he saw Ansh's chin tremble?
qa.a: It suggests he felt ashamed, recognising the same hurt he feels when Seema mocks him in front of guests.

qa.q: What was the wise change Suraj made?
qa.a: He noticed the hurt on Ansh's face, stopped straight away, gave back the cap and apologised.

qa.q: How might Ansh see Suraj's apology?
qa.a: Ansh may be wary and unsure it is real, since he takes the cap without saying anything.

grounding: A boy mocks a quieter boy to feel big, echoing how his cousin treats him at home; he notices the hurt on the boy's face, stops and apologises.
